# LLM post-training by institution, company, or university

[简体中文](../../../post-training/catalog/by-organization.md) · English

Grouped by the first listed affiliation of the first author, with newest first within each group. Each paper includes the first author's name and a short method description. Joint work is not repeated under every collaborator.

## AMAP, Alibaba Group

- 2026-08-24 · First author: Xianlei Zhou · [Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization](../../../post-training/2608.23311-erpo/README-en.md) (`erpo`): ERPO observes that the induced query distribution also drifts during RL, so it puts regularization on the input side. Frozen-reference query likelihood gives static query weights; Query-KL controls environment-distribution drift without directly constraining the response score function.

## Affiliation not listed in the paper

- 2026-08-27 · First author: Ivan Kruzhilov · [Disentangling Optimization Scale from Preference Scale in DPO](../../../post-training/2608.27032-normalized-dpo/README-en.md) (`normalized-dpo`): Standard DPO beta changes preference noise and gradient size simultaneously, implicitly scaling learning rate. Divide a centered softplus by beta to preserve the minimizer and keep nonvanishing gradient in the beta-to-zero limit.

## Alibaba / Qwen

- 2026-08-04 · First author: Wen Wang · [SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation](../../../post-training/2608.03092-smopd/README-en.md) (`smopd`): Train specialist teachers with reward priorities, then merge their capabilities on the student's own trajectories.

## Alibaba Cloud Computing

- 2026-10-15 · First author: Bingxi Hou · [Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation](../../../post-training/2610.21601-waypoint-opd/README-en.md) (`waypoint-opd`): Student top-k chooses the candidates. Early and late shifts are centered by the student weights on those candidates; the positive cosine then scales the endpoint credit. **Bounded component only; full experiments are not reproduced.**

## Alibaba DAMO Academy

- 2023-04-11 · First author: Zheng Yuan · [RRHF](../../../post-training/2304.05302-rrhf/README-en.md) (`rrhf`): PPO-RLHF coordinates policy, old policy, reward and value models, making training and tuning complex. RRHF samples responses from several models or humans, uses reward to rank them all, aligns the model's average log-likelihood order with reward order, and applies SFT to the highest-quality answer.

## Alibaba Group

- 2026-10-16 · First author: Yuhan Sun · [MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation](../../../post-training/2610.23234-multiagent-opd/README-en.md) (`multiagent-opd`): The Leader learns from team outcomes; the Answerer learns from its own candidate's correctness. See Section 3. **Not reproduced due to cost (review complete); research material only, no executable entry.**
- 2026-10-09 · First author: Zhentao Zhang · [State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents](../../../reproductions/2610.13238-state-opd/README-en.md) (`state-opd`): Full-vocabulary entropy selects states for extra complete reasoning-and-action samples, whose actions are not executed. The implementation keeps Appendix D.1's actual sampled-K1 dual clipping, not a scoring heuristic.
- 2026-10-08 · First author: Fei Ding · [When KL Regularization Misfires in Group Policy Optimization](../../../post-training/2610.12161-zcpo/README-en.md) (`zcpo`): Independent KL penalties may update policy despite tied rewards or canceling reward gradients. Center response-average conditional KL within the group and put it in the frozen reward coefficient, not a standalone loss.
- 2026-10-01 · First author: Yihua Zhu · [My FAULT: Self-Diagnosis as Credit Assignment in Self-Evolving Agentic Reinforcement Learning](../../../post-training/2610.01161-my-fault/README-en.md) (`my-fault`): Only claims verified by evidence enter online error pricing. Learned relative costs redistribute terminal credit to steps while conserving its total.
- 2026-09-15 · First author: Zishuo Zhao · [Turn-level Multiscale Density Ratio Estimation for LLM Agents](../../../post-training/2609.16760-tlm-dre/README-en.md) (`tlm-dre`): Allocate weights at multiple scales by conversation turn, and use asymmetric token updates for positive and negative density ratios.
- 2025-08-15 · First author: Wenhao Zhang · [CHORD](../../../post-training/2508.11408-chord/README-en.md) (`chord`): Separate SFT and RL stages can overfit expert data or forget it too early. Add expert SFT as an annealed auxiliary term during on-policy RL; token-level uncertainty weights smooth the transition from imitation to exploration.
- 2025-08-11 · First author: Zhenpeng Su · [GPPO](../../../post-training/2508.07629-gppo/README-en.md) (`gppo`): This can suppress exploration and learning from negative samples. GPPO keeps PPO's forward clipped objective while restoring backward signals in those regions with a stop-gradient boundary weight.

## Alibaba Qwen Team

- 2025-12-01 · First author: Chujie Zheng · [Stabilizing RL with LLMs](../../../post-training/2512.01374-minirl/README-en.md) (`minirl`): Separate train–inference mismatch from policy staleness. Use on-policy importance correction and combine off-policy clipping with MoE Routing Replay.
- 2025-07-24 · First author: Chujie Zheng · [GSPO](../../../post-training/2507.18071-gspo/README-en.md) (`gspo`): GSPO averages the log-ratios for a response, then exponentiates the result to get one sequence ratio. The entire sequence shares the clipping weight.

## AllSpark Team

- 2026-09-22 · First author: Jiayan Fu · [PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment](../../../post-training/2609.26355-pact/README-en.md) (`pact`): Update the actor first so the critic targets the updated policy. Using a current-token ratio rather than the product over the remaining sequence is a first-order approximation, not exact continuation importance sampling.

## AllSpark Team (team byline; no institution listed)

- 2026-09-28 · First author: AllSpark Team · [ROSS: Relearning from Self-Generated Rollouts through Selective Supervision](../../../post-training/2609.35954-ross/README-en.md) (`ross`): Keep the full context of historical self-rollouts but compute loss only on selected model continuations, avoiding imitation of erroneous or redundant steps.

## Amazon / Duke University

- 2026-09-03 · First author: Zhishuai Liu · [Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability](../../../post-training/2609.04565-sparse-opd/README-en.md) (`sparse-opd`): Instead of supervising every generated token, choose one or two key positions (about 0.05%). Largest positive differences work particularly well, suggesting targeted correction rather than word-for-word matching.

## Anhui Province Key Laboratory of Digital Security

- 2026-10-13 · First author: Wei Fan · [LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers](../../../reproductions/2610.18162-loopsd/README-en.md) (`loopsd`): On-policy self-distillation needs a more useful teacher than the student, but that does not have to be a bigger external model or additional answer context. LoOPSD searches for contiguous blocks of layers to repeat without changing the weights, uses that route as the teacher for student-generated prefixes, and searches for a new teacher after the student update. **Not reproduced for now due to cost; validation pending, no executable entry.**

## Ant Group

- 2025-12-16 · First author: Jian Hu · [Online IcePop](../../../post-training/web-2025-online-icepop/README-en.md) (`online-icepop`): Online IcePop allows only one update per batch, so the stale-policy ratio is 1 and PPO ratio/clipping are removed. Keep the IcePop two-sided mask and original in-range engine-mismatch ratio.
- 2025-10-21 · First author: Ling Team · [IcePop](../../../post-training/2510.18855-icepop/README-en.md) (`icepop`): One-sided TIS may retain very small mismatched ratios. Mask ratios outside a fixed two-sided interval and retain original corrections inside.

## Anthropic

- 2022-12-15 · First author: Yuntao Bai · [Constitutional AI](../../../post-training/2212.08073-constitutional-ai/README-en.md) (`constitutional-ai`): In stage one, the model critiques and rewrites its responses according to the principles, then learns by SFT on the revisions. In stage two, AI compares responses, a preference model is trained, and its reward drives RLAIF.

## Apple

- 2025-06-30 · First author: Bo Liu · [SPIRAL](../../../post-training/2506.24119-spiral/README-en.md) (`spiral`): The same model plays problem setter and solver. Automatically scored zero-sum multiround games create a progressively harder curriculum.

## Arizona State University / University of Virginia / Stevens Institute of Technology

- 2026-09-15 · First author: Chenhao Qiu · [OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation](../../../post-training/2609.16459-opd-aha/README-en.md) (`opd-aha`): Reconstruct a visually preferred target from the difference between the teacher's distributions with actual and empty visual input. This counters momentum from an incorrect linguistic prefix.

## Australian Institute for Machine Learning, Adelaide University / StepFun

- 2026-11-02 · First author: Sinuo Wang · [P²-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors](../../../post-training/2611.03953-p2-mopd/README-en.md) (`p2-mopd`): Free weights can leave their span; coefficient gradients explicitly move along expert directions. Inference capacity does not increase, and coefficients fold into ordinary exported weights. **Bounded component only; full experiments are not reproduced.**

## Authors did not disclose affiliation

- 2026-08-19 · First author: Chen Yang · [Beyond Imitation: Filtering On-Policy Distillation by Reasoning Progress](../../../post-training/2608.19408-r2-opd/README-en.md) (`r2-opd`): Rank reasoning spans by teacher reward and an independent progress reward. Mask distillation where those rankings conflict.
- 2026-08-04 · First author: Jian Zhang · [CausalOPD: First-Wrong-Step Supervision for Distilling Causal Chain Reasoning](../../../post-training/2608.03673-causal-opd/README-en.md) (`causal-opd`): The teacher identifies the first incorrect step in the on-policy causal chain, repairs it with short-horizon RL, and advances the curriculum from evidence through mechanism to conclusion.
- 2026-07-30 · First author: Xingjian Wu · [Contrastive Reinforced Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation](../../../post-training/2607.28026-crpo/README-en.md) (`crpo`): Use predictive entropy to distinguish positive reflection/exploration positions from negative exposure-bias positions, then contrast privileged self-distillation signals within groups.
- 2026-07-29 · First author: Jianze Wang · [SERPO: Self-Evolving Rubric Policy Optimization for Open-Ended Test-Time Reinforcement Learning](../../../post-training/2607.26873-serpo/README-en.md) (`serpo`): A Good–Normal–Bad response archive, query-specific rubrics and actor policy co-evolve in a three-way feedback loop.

## Baidu Inc.

- 2026-10-19 · First author: Shiao Xie · [Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation](../../../post-training/2610.26856-vag/README-en.md) (`visually-attributable-opd`): It keeps corrections aligned with the visual contrast and uses a bounded term to modulate the verifier's group-normalized advantage. A text-only teacher or fixed-logit gate would not implement this multimodal path. **Not reproduced due to cost (review complete); research material only, no executable entry.**

## Beihang University

- 2026-10-15 · First author: Xiuhui Zhang · [Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models](../../../post-training/2610.22056-progress-reward/README-en.md) (`progress-reward`): It uses the subtask's semantics as a state prior and the difference in progress between successive states as dense reward for low-level RL. The plan is generated in advance; the LLM does not run at every environment step. **Bounded component only; full experiments are not reproduced.**

## Beijing Institute of Technology

- 2026-05-13 · First author: Feng Zhang · [ConSPO](../../../post-training/2605.12969-conspo/README-en.md) (`conspo`): Express preferences among sequences in the same group as length-normalized InfoNCE, avoiding length and within-group scale biases caused by summing token scores.

## ByteDance Seed

- 2025-04-07 · First author: Yu Yue · [VAPO](../../../post-training/2504.05118-vapo/README-en.md) (`vapo`): Critic bias, heterogeneous lengths and sparse rewards destabilize value-based PPO on long traces. VAPO pretrains a value model and adapts GAE and actor updates to response length.
- 2025-03-18 · First author: Qiying Yu · [DAPO](../../../post-training/2503.14476-dapo/README-en.md) (`dapo`): Standard symmetric clipping can suppress exploration in online RL for long chains of thought, and groups with all correct or all wrong answers offer no learning signal. DAPO's Clip-Higher gives more room to increase probabilities; Dynamic Sampling discards zero-variance groups; token-level loss handles responses of different lengths fairly; and overlong responses receive a piecewise penalty.

## ByteDance internship

- 2026-07-28 · First author: Bo-Wen Zhang · [CoRT](../../../post-training/2607.25659-cort/README-en.md) (`cort`): Replay the same response with a rubric and with criteria removed. Token likelihood differences redistribute GRPO's response-level advantage.

## Carnegie Mellon University

- 2026-10-27 · First author: Jixuan Leng · [CONCUR: Concordant Auxiliary Rewards for Multi-Task, Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning](../../../post-training/2610.36437-concur/README-en.md) (`concur`): CONCUR-T always ties auxiliary scores at the primary-reward ceiling. CONCUR-A relaxes that tie once cumulative agreement meets a threshold. **Bounded component only; full experiments are not reproduced.**
- 2026-04-17 · First author: Jixuan Leng · [GroupDPO: Memory-Efficient Group-Wise Direct Preference Optimization](../../../post-training/2604.15602-group-dpo/README-en.md) (`group-dpo`): Section 4, Algorithm 1 and Table 1 in v1/v2 were reviewed; no material difference was found for these objectives. The implementation follows pinned v2, including accumulation for responses shared across groups. **Bounded component only; full experiments are not reproduced.**

## Chongqing University

- 2026-09-10 · First author: Bincheng Gu · [Beyond Confidence: Stability-Aware Test-Time Adaptation for LLM Reasoning](../../../post-training/2609.11393-tasco/README-en.md) (`tasco`): Freeze the base model and optimize a lightweight prefix. Penalize instability under neighborhood perturbations as well as low confidence, to avoid confident but incorrect trajectories.

## City University of Hong Kong

- 2026-10-22 · First author: Xuyang Zhong · [MOER: Mix-Policy Optimization under Expert Prefix Guidance with Selective Rollback](../../../post-training/2610.30873-moer/README-en.md) (`moer`): The whole guided trajectory, including student-generated suffix, is off-policy. Rollback avoids an additional generation, not the original generation/verifier cost. **Bounded component only; full experiments are not reproduced.**

## Cohere For AI

- 2024-02-22 · First author: Arash Ahmadian · [RLOO](../../../post-training/2402.14740-rloo/README-en.md) (`rloo`): RLOO treats a full response as one action. Sample several responses for the same prompt and use the other responses' mean reward as the current one’s baseline.

## Contextual AI

- 2024-02-02 · First author: Kawin Ethayarajh · [KTO](../../../post-training/2402.01306-kto/README-en.md) (`kto`): It uses the expected KL between policy and reference as a reference point. Examples of each class can be collected independently and need not be balanced.

## Cornell University

- 2026-10-16 · First author: Wen-Zhi Li · [Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay](../../../post-training/2610.24236-tar-adaptive-replay/README-en.md) (`tar-adaptive-replay`): This avoids continuously imitating a limited bank at the expense of adaptation. - 2026-10-15 · First author: Zhengxin Zhang · [Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?](../../../post-training/2610.21337-stopd/README-en.md) (`stopd`): Every retained token receives teacher supervision weighted by its exact inclusion probability; natural EOS is an ordinary valid token. Dividing by the current batch's random token count would invalidate the gradient-sum argument, so training uses the previous batch's weighted token count. **Bounded component only; full experiments are not reproduced.**

## Cursor Research / UC Berkeley

- 2026-11-03 · First author: Kevin Frans · [Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning](../../../post-training/2611.05266-targeted-guidance/README-en.md) (`targeted-guidance`): The same policy under that feedback becomes a stop-gradient teacher while the student learns on its own actual history. The defining combination is **minimal, failed-turn-gated direction plus ordinary per-criterion RL reward**, not unrestricted whole-trajectory OPSD, to reduce diversity pressure and primary-task interference. **Bounded component only; full experiments are not reproduced.**

## Dalian Maritime University

- 2026-10-09 · First author: Ronghan Li · [A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO](../../../reproductions/2610.13669-grpo-difficulty-curriculum/README-en.md) (`grpo-difficulty-curriculum`): Advancing to B5 can hurt results. This implementation reestimates difficulty from actual rollouts at every step, retains B5 as a control, and does not substitute problem length or stale scores.

## Dalian University of Technology / Kuaishou

- 2026-09-29 · First author: Youling Huang · [Guide, Then Let Go: Gap-Adaptive Teacher Scheduling for Sparse-Reward Agentic RL](../../../post-training/2609.37898-gats/README-en.md) (`gats`): OPD weight decreases linearly as the gap closes. Once the student reaches the teacher reference, turn off teacher supervision permanently and continue with GRPO alone.

## DeepSeek-AI

- 2024-02-05 · First author: Zhihong Shao · [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md) (`grpo`): GRPO samples a group of responses to each question and computes advantages from the group's reward mean and standard deviation, removing the critic. ## Duke University

- 2026-11-03 · First author: Qingyuan Zheng · [Shuffled OPSD: When Semantic Consistency Hurts On-Policy Self-Distillation?](../../../post-training/2611.04958-shuffled-opsd/README-en.md) (`shuffled-opsd`): The same transformation conditions student generation and teacher scoring. ## East China Normal University

- 2026-10-08 · First author: Zipeng Wang · [MetaOPD: Meta-Learned Token Weighting for On-Policy Distillation](../../../post-training/2610.11989-meta-opd/README-en.md) (`meta-opd`): A lightweight network learns token supervision weights from student and teacher predictions. ## Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo / The Hong Kong Polytechnic University

- 2026-10-08 · First author: Anhao Zhao · [DIAL-OPD: Learning More from Fewer Tokens in On-Policy Distillation](../../../post-training/2610.11659-dial-opd/README-en.md) (`dial-opd`): A logarithmic probability mean reduces supervision priority for tokens that both teacher and student consider unlikely. Rank positions separately per response; unselected positions remain in the context.

- 2026-07-28 · First author: Pierre Chambon · [Reinforcement Learning for Code Optimization](../../../post-training/2607.25970-code-optimization-rl/README-en.md) (`code-optimization-rl`): Offline replay selects rewards and environments; online GRPO addresses sparse rewards and stale batches. See Sections 3–5 and Appendices C–F. **Not reproduced due to cost (review complete); research material only, no executable entry.**

## Fudan University

- 2026-08-27 · First author: Siye Wu · [Consolidating RLVR Capabilities Across Domains: A Deep Dive into Fusion Paradigms](../../../post-training/2608.27409-rlvr-fusion/README-en.md) (`rlvr-fusion`): The paper compares three cross-domain capability fusion paradigms that reuse different artifacts: Merge combines expert task vectors, Mix RL combines training data, and MOPD reuses both experts and data. Average differences are at most 1.4 points but can reach 8.6 points on individual tasks, so the choice depends on expert availability, data, and cost.

## Georgia Institute of Technology

- 2026-09-30 · First author: Xinchen Du · [SHARPO: Segment-Level Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning](../../../post-training/2610.00838-sharpo/README-en.md) (`sharpo`): Use a successful trajectory from the same group as self-distillation context. - 2026-09-29 · First author: Zhiqi Li · [FlowMap-OPD: Rollout-Kernel Separation for On-Policy Distillation of Few-Step Flow-Map Generators](../../../post-training/2609.37851-flowmap-opd/README-en.md) (`flowmap-opd`): Rollout supplies states with the correct marginal distribution. ## Google

- 2026-10-23 · First author: Leon Sick · [On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models](../../../post-training/2610.32770-opst/README-en.md) (`opst`): Discard a too-easy item only if all $G$ student rollouts match the proposed answer; agreement on some other answer is not sufficient. - 2025-09-30 · First author: Zhuohang Li · [Judging with Confidence: Calibrating Autoraters to Preference Distributions](../../../post-training/2510.00263-probabilistic-autorater/README-en.md) (`probabilistic-autorater`): The strict local tag parser is an explicit local choice, not the unpublished author parser. - 2023-10-18 · First author: Mohammad Gheshlaghi Azar · [IPO](../../../post-training/2310.12036-ipo/README-en.md) (`ipo`): The paper proposes $\Psi$PO, which optimizes preference probabilities directly. - 2023-06-23 · First author: Rishabh Agarwal · [GKD](../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en.md) (`gkd`): GKD lets the student generate rollouts from its current policy and queries the teacher for full distributions at the states the student actually visits.
